findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The CI-reuse drain test would make real git push and gh calls to GitHub. The insteadOf redirect the plan relies on does not exist, and early_seam is cfg(test) only.
findings.evidence: Both cases give the test repo the origin `https://github.com/owner/repo`, which runs `push_ci_branch` and `early_pr` before the checks. Outside cfg(test), and the drain tests build athena-core without it, `with_ci_remote` uses a real `GitRemote` on origin, and `early_pr_to` uses the real `GhCli` (gh/early.rs:447). `early_seam` is cfg(test) only (gh/mod.rs:77). No `insteadOf` appears anywhere under crates/, and drain.rs has no GitHub origin at all. So the test would push to github.com, call the real `gh` for the early PR, and delete a real branch at close. That is an external service, with no state named and no way to check or wait for it. Fix: Widen `early_seam` (gh/mod.rs, gh/early.rs) to cfg(any(test, feature="test-support")) the same way as ci_seam, and give test_support an installer for a fake Remote and PrHost. Name these two files as extra deliverables and give the reason. Write case (b) with no origin, which needs no seam.

findings.summary: Checking resume.json for the substring "verifier" is fragile. Parse the mark instead.
findings.evidence: ResumeMark (state.rs:398) also serializes the candidate, report_gaps and left_criteria, all free text that can contain the word 'verifier'. Fix: Deserialize into `ResumeMark` (or use `StateDir::read_resume`) and test `stage == ResumeStage::Verifier`.

findings.summary: The conditional scope_guard.rs edit falls outside the deliverables.
findings.evidence: Athena already flagged that this file is not a deliverable. Fix: Change the test_support helper in a way that keeps scope_guard's test passing unchanged. If the file must change anyway, say why in the change description.

findings.summary: The 'fails without' text for criterion 5 is confusing.
findings.evidence: It describes how the helper change could break things, not a missing behavior. Criterion 5 is a no-regression check. Fix: Say plainly that this is a regression check: the existing disk-hold tests must keep passing.

summary: I read run/mod.rs, run/checks.rs, routing.rs, gh/early.rs, state.rs and the drain.rs and binary.rs helpers. The core design is sound and fixes the fault where it starts. Moving `disk_gate` into `SnapExec::exec` behind a once flag gates only right before a local check. A green or red CI result, a resumed job and a nested run never call `exec`. The LowDisk error does pass up unchanged: `run_local` uses `?`, `Fallback` stores the original error and `Outcome::Blocked` returns it, so `check_and_verify` can downcast it and call the existing `hold_for_disk`. The criterion 1 test would fail under the old order. Moving the helpers' 'checks done' signal to the resume mark is needed. One major problem stops acceptance. The CI-reuse drain test needs a GitHub origin. In the integration-test build that origin drives a real `git push` and real `gh` early-PR calls, because `early_seam` is cfg(test) only. The `insteadOf` setting the plan relies on does not exist in the fixtures. The plan must widen `early_seam` and name those files. Smaller fixes: parse the resume mark instead of matching a substring, and keep the scope_guard change conditional.
